# Agent Configuration for pi-coding-agent

You live inside a docker with ollama. If you want to install a package you need to update `/home/sabeiro/lav/src/blender_cv/mcp_server/ollama/Dockerfile`

## Models
Available models (see models.list):
- llama3.2:1b (default small model)
- llama3.1:8b (medium)
- llama3:8b
- mistral-7b-v0.3
- phi-3-mini-4k
- qwen2.5-7b-instruct

## Recommended Usage
```bash
# Chat with agent
ollama llama3.2:1b "Implement this feature"

# Pull all recommended models
ollama pull llama3.2:1b llama3.1:8b mistral-7b-v0.3
```

## Integration
Available functions:
- `ollama chat` - Interactive chat
- `ollama run` - Run specific model
- MCP protocol for Emacs integration

## Troubleshooting
```bash
# Check container
docker compose ps

# Check logs
docker compose logs -f

# Pull model
docker exec -it ollama ollama pull llama3.2:1b
```

if docker ps grep ollama &>/dev/null; then
    OLLAMA_MODEL="${OLLAMA_MODEL:-llama3.2:1b}"

content.text:
# project scope

This project allows the running of local agents as supporters. Those agents will be used for supporting the development of FEM/blender integration, energy optimization engines and CV/ML on embedded devices.

- goal :: a local coding assistant
- stack :: IDE: emacs, LLM serve: ollama, OS: ubuntu 26
- workflow :: within emacs, code will be executed via python REPL and .org code blocks
- purpose :: data analytics, no need for production code, simple and readable code, avoid abstraction
- test :: no successful results without testing and documenting
- language :: the project language is English, don't translate
- config :: python programs uses json files as config, run logs will be added to that json and saved into a `runs/` folder for versioning

# project structure

Project structure :

- assistants :: coding assistants
  - [[./agent_call.org][agent_call.org]] :: detailed agent instructions to run this project and to explain it's outpt
  - [[./aider/][aider/]] :: conf files to use with aider
  - [[./config.json][config.json]] :: the pi-coding-agent config file
  - [[./emacs][emacs]] :: conf files for agentic usage of emacs in org mode
- deployment ::
  - [[./ansible/][ansible/]] :: ansible script for remote deployment (i.e. jetson)
  - [[./docker-compose.yml][docker-compose.yml]] :: to start mcp_server and mcp_client
  - [[./logs/][logs/]] :: application outputs for debugging
  - [[./nginx/][nginx/]] :: web server configuration to deploy this project (i.e. on jetson)
  - [[./ollama/][ollama/]] :: ollama container and conf
  - [[./mcphub/][mcphub/]] :: to monitor mcp applications
  - [[./morpheus/][morpheus/]] :: nvidia onnx cybersecurity ML enrichment on cuda
  - [[./test/][test/]] :: collection of script to test the configurations
- apps ::
  - [[./blender_mcp/][blender_mcp]] :: definition of the mcp addon to integrate with blender
  - [[./mcp-client/][mcp-client]] :: app to interact with the mcp-server
  - [[./mcp-server/][mcp-server/]] :: app exposing the mcp tools for the language models mainly consumed by gptel
- context ::
  - [[./doc/][doc/]] :: machine generated documentation of useful components
- presentation ::
  - [[./html/][html]] :: slides and diagrams to present the project
  - [[./icon][icon/]] :: useful icons for the presentation
  - [[./img/][img/]] :: images for the documentation
  - [[./html/js/][js/]] :: javascript for the presentation
  - [[./html/css/][css/]] :: style sheets for professional technical documentation
  - [[./data/][data/]] :: input data like json graphs
  - [[./script/][script/]] :: collection of script to run this project

# agent

- local  :: you are developing local applications for pilot test, no need to over engineer the project
- docker :: the applications run locally or in docker, no need for virtual env

# project outcome

- this project provides agentic support to data scientists. The LLMs run locally with ollama, both on ubuntu with Nvidia GPU
- the data scientists need to build an MCP server to allow their programming to interact with different systems:
  - [[./blender-mcp/][blender-mcp/]] :: blender for 3d modeling
  - [[../heat_fem/][heat_fem/]] :: fenics/doplhin for FEM calculation
  - [[../phys_opt/][phys_opt]] :: optimization engine for graphs
  - [[../pose_estimate_py/][pose_estimate_py]] :: computer vision (pose estimate)
  - knowledge graphs

#  web/UI specs

Web pages should be produced with:

- Audience :: scientific/technical blog
- Theme :: dark, elegant, simple, readable
- Layout :: centered and long sections should be collapsable.
- CSS :: use classes to be addressed in style sheets 
- JS :: minimal usage, ideally none
- images :: centered with a opaque background and some shadow
- headers :: h1, h2,h3... should have similar shades but different and elegant
- navbar :: minimal, few links, elegant, discrete
- printable :: the output should be able to produce pdf, no button
- footer :: put intertino as owner and license [[https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-sa/4.0/][CC by-nc-sa]] 

# tech stack

The main libraries:

- python: ollama, mcp
- js: d3.js
- web: html/css

# hardware

The project is optimized to run locally on:

1. Laptop [[https://www.acer.com/us-en/laptops/nitro/nitro-v-16-ai-amd][ACER nitro V16 AI]]:
   - CPU: AMD Ryzen 7 with NPU
   - GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060
   - RAM: 32GB 
2. [[https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/autonomous-machines/embedded-systems/jetson-orin/nano-super-developer-kit/][Nvidia Jetson orin nano]]:
   - 2x ARM Cortex-A55 cores
   - RAM: 8GB

# Jetson CV - Computer Vision on NVIDIA Jetson

Real-time computer vision application for NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano, featuring pose estimation with TensorRT acceleration and gamepad/MIDI controller support.

## Project Structure

```
cv/
├── camera/           # Runtime application (TensorRT inference)
├── pose_estimate_py/ # Model training and export (ultralytics/PyTorch)
├── pose_estimate_of/ # OpenFrameworks C++ implementation
├── model/            # Saved models (.onnx, .engine, .pt)
├── media/            # Saved media files (photos, videos)
└── script/           # Setup utilities for Jetson
```

## Folders

### `camera/` - Runtime Application
Production runtime using TensorRT for GPU-accelerated inference. No PyTorch required.

- **camera_controller.py** - Main application with camera, pose estimation, and controller support
- **controllers.py** - Gamepad (USB/Bluetooth), MIDI, and keyboard input handling
- **controller_config.json** - Input mappings configuration

**Features:**
- CSI camera support (IMX219, etc.)
- Real-time pose estimation (YOLO)
- Zoom, pan, flip controls
- Photo/video capture
- Histogram and vectorscope display

### `pose_estimate_py/` - Training & Export
Development environment for training and exporting models using ultralytics.

- Train custom pose models
- Export to ONNX format for TensorRT

```python
# Export model for runtime use
from ultralytics import YOLO
model = YOLO('yolo11n-pose.pt')
model.export(format='onnx')
# Copy .onnx file to model/ folder
```

### `model/` - Saved Models
Store trained models here:
- `.pt` - PyTorch models (for training/export)
- `.onnx` - ONNX models (for TensorRT conversion)
- `.engine` - TensorRT engines (auto-generated, cached)

### `media/` - Saved Media
Output directory for captured photos and recorded videos.

### `script/` - Setup Utilities
Shell scripts for Jetson setup:
- OpenCV CUDA build script
- Package installation for ARM architecture
- Environment configuration

## Quick Start

### 1. Setup Jetson Environment

```bash
# Add to ~/.bashrc
export CUDA_HOME=/usr/local/cuda
export PATH=$CUDA_HOME/bin:$PATH
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=$CUDA_HOME/lib64:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH
export CPATH=$CUDA_HOME/include:$CPATH

source ~/.bashrc
```

### 2. Install Dependencies

```bash
# System packages
sudo apt install python3-opencv python3-numpy

# Python packages
cd camera
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

### 3. Enable CSI Camera

```bash
sudo /opt/nvidia/jetson-io/jetson-io.py
# Select your camera, reboot
```

### 4. Run

```bash
cd camera
python -m camera.camera_controller
```

## Controller Support

| Input | Support |
|-------|---------|
| Keyboard | Built-in (OpenCV) |
| USB Gamepad | pygame |
| Bluetooth Gamepad | evdev |
| MIDI Controller | python-rtmidi |

Edit `camera/controller_config.json` to customize button mappings.

## Requirements

- NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano (JetPack 6.x)
- CSI Camera (IMX219 or compatible)
- Python 3.10+
- TensorRT (pre-installed with JetPack)
- CUDA 12.x (pre-installed with JetPack)

## License

MIT

**Prototype project** for on-premises digital twin systems using NVIDIA Jetson hardware, local AI inference, and FEM/physics simulations. **No cloud providers** - fully on-prem solution using local Ollama instances and Jetson Orin Nano for edge computing.

## Architecture

## Hardware Requirements

### Required Hardware
- **NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano** (4GB/8GB RAM) - Primary deployment target
- **CSI Camera** (IMX219 or compatible) - Real-time vision input
- **NVIDIA RTX 5060** (desktop) - Alternative for offline rendering
- **NVMe SSD** - Fast storage for models, logs, data streams

### Supported Devices
- NVIDIA JetPack 6.x (Orin Nano/AM4)
- Raspberry Pi Pico/Zero 2 W (edge nodes)
- M5Stack with sensors
- ESP32 IoT devices (MQTT broker nodes)
- PC workstations (rendering, FEM analysis)

### Minimum Resources
- **RAM:** 8GB (Jetson), 16GB (PC)
- **GPU:** 4GB+ CUDA cores
- **CPU:** Quad-core minimum
- **Storage:** 32GB SSD (expandable to 1TB+ for media)

---

## Core Components

### 1. Computer Vision Pipeline (`camera_py/`, `camera/`)

Real-time pose estimation using TensorRT-accelerated models:

- **pose_estimate_py/** - PyTorch/Ultralytics training & export
  - Train custom pose models with YOLO11n-pose
  - Export to ONNX for TensorRT conversion
  - Batch processing with queue management

- **pose_estimate_of/** - OpenFrameworks C++ for high-performance inference
  - ONNX runtime integration
  - Low-latency deployment

- **model/** - Model artifacts storage:
  - `.pt` - PyTorch models (training)
  - `.onnx` - ONNX Intermediate format
  - `.engine` - TensorRT optimized engines

**Features:**
- CSI camera support (IMX219, RGB, thermal)
- Real-time inference (≤100ms latency)
- Zoom, pan, flip controls
- Photo/video capture
- Histogram and vectorscope displays

### 2. Finite Element Analysis (`heat_fem/`)

Thermal and structural simulations using FEniCSx/DOLPHIN:

- **FEM Mesh** - Adaptive mesh refinement
- **Thermal Analysis** - Heat transfer, conduction, radiation
- **Structural** - Stress, strain, deformation
- **Optimization** - Topology optimization for lightweight designs

**Features:**
- HDF5 output for large datasets
- 30-minute solver timeout
- Mesh quality validation
- Parallel computation (8 cores max)

### 3. Physics Optimization (`phys_opt/`)

Constraint-based optimization engines:

- **Pyomo** - Mathematical modeling
- **IPOPT** - Interior-point optimization
- **Result caching** - 24-hour cache
- **Multi-physics** - Thermal + structural + fluid

### 4. Visualization & 3D (`blender_cv/`, `video_to_3d/`)

3D modeling and rendering:

- **Blender integration** - 3D scene assembly
- **ONNX models** - Direct export to 3D
- **WebGL** - Web-based 3D viewers
- **Export formats** - .obj, .fbx, .glb

### 5. IoT & Sensor Integration

Real-world data ingestion:

- **MQTT** - MQTT broker for sensor pub/sub
- **OPC-UA** - Industrial device integration
- **CoAP** - Lightweight MQTT alternative
- **Sensor fusion** - Multi-sensor data merging
- **Data streams** - High-frequency telemetry

### 6. Edge Computing & Deployment

On-prem deployment capabilities:

- **JetPack 6.x** - NVIDIA accelerated runtime
- **TensorRT** - GPU-accelerated inference
- **ONNX Runtime** - CPU GPU interoperability
- **Model optimization** - Quantization, pruning for edge
- **Docker/Kubernetes** - Container orchestration
- **sys_sync.sh** - System synchronization script

---

## On-Prem Architecture

### Network Design
```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐
│    ON-PREM ONLY - No Cloud Connection    │
├──────────────────────────────────────────┤

│  │ NVMe SSD    │                        │
│  │ Storage     │                        │
│  └─────────────┘                        │
└──────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Security
- **No SSH** from untrusted networks
- **Container isolation** for all services
- **Read-only** file permissions on shared volumes
- **Local LLM** only (Ollama - no API keys)
- **No external** database connections

---

## Digital Twin Capabilities

### What's Included
- **Visual Twin** - 3D models from Blender + pose estimation
- **Physical Twin** - FEM + physics simulations + multi-physics
- **Sensing Twin** - IoT integration, real-time data streams
- **Intelligent Twin** - ML models, knowledge graphs, predictive analytics

## Hardware Requirements

- Raspberry Pi Pico/Zero 2 W (edge nodes)

## Core Components

### 1. Computer Vision Pipeline (`camera_py/`, `camera/`)

Real-time pose estimation using TensorRT-accelerated models:

- **pose_estimate_py/** - PyTorch/Ultralytics training & export
  - Train custom pose models with YOLO11n-pose
  - Export to ONNX for TensorRT conversion
  - Batch processing with queue management

- **pose_estimate_of/** - OpenFrameworks C++ for high-performance inference
  - ONNX runtime integration
  - Low-latency deployment

- **model/** - Model artifacts storage:
  - `.pt` - PyTorch models (training)
  - `.onnx` - ONNX Intermediate format
  - `.engine` - TensorRT optimized engines

**Features:**
- CSI camera support (IMX219, RGB, thermal)
- Real-time inference (≤100ms latency)
- Zoom, pan, flip controls
- Photo/video capture
- Histogram and vectorscope displays

### 2. Finite Element Analysis (`heat_fem/`)

Thermal and structural simulations using FEniCSx/DOLPHIN:

- **FEM Mesh** - Adaptive mesh refinement
- **Thermal Analysis** - Heat transfer, conduction, radiation
- **Structural** - Stress, strain, deformation
- **Optimization** - Topology optimization for lightweight designs

**Features:**
- HDF5 output for large datasets
- 30-minute solver timeout
- Mesh quality validation
- Parallel computation (8 cores max)

### 3. Physics Optimization (`phys_opt/`)

Constraint-based optimization engines:

- **Pyomo** - Mathematical modeling
- **IPOPT** - Interior-point optimization
- **Result caching** - 24-hour cache
- **Multi-physics** - Thermal + structural + fluid

### 4. Visualization & 3D (`blender_cv/`, `video_to_3d/`)

3D modeling and rendering:

- **Blender integration** - 3D scene assembly
- **ONNX models** - Direct export to 3D
- **WebGL** - Web-based 3D viewers
- **Export formats** - .obj, .fbx, .glb

### 5. IoT & Sensor Integration

Real-world data ingestion:

- **MQTT** - MQTT broker for sensor pub/sub
- **OPC-UA** - Industrial device integration
- **CoAP** - Lightweight MQTT alternative
- **Sensor fusion** - Multi-sensor data merging
- **Data streams** - High-frequency telemetry

### 6. Edge Computing & Deployment

On-prem deployment capabilities:

- **JetPack 6.x** - NVIDIA accelerated runtime
- **TensorRT** - GPU-accelerated inference
- **ONNX Runtime** - CPU GPU interoperability
- **Model optimization** - Quantization, pruning for edge
- **Docker/Kubernetes** - Container orchestration
- **sys_sync.sh** - System synchronization script

## Quick Start

### 1. Environment Setup

```bash
# Load CUDA environment
export CUDA_HOME=/usr/local/cuda
export PATH=$CUDA_HOME/bin:$PATH
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=$CUDA_HOME/lib64:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH
export CPATH=$CUDA_HOME/include:$CPATH

source ~/.bashrc
```

### 2. Install Dependencies

```bash
# System packages
sudo apt install python3-opencv python3-numpy

# Python packages
cd camera
pip install -r requirements.txt

# Configure camera (CSI)
sudo /opt/nvidia/jetson-io/jetson-io.py
```

### 3. Build Models

```bash
# Train pose model
cd pose_estimate_py
python train.py

# Export to ONNX
model.export(format='onnx')
mv model.onnx ../model/

# Create TensorRT engine
cd ../camera
python build_engine.py
```

### 4. Run Application

```bash
cd camera
python -m camera.camera_controller

# Or use Docker
docker compose up -d
```

### 5. Deploy Digital Twin

```bash
# Start all services
docker compose up -d

# Check status
docker compose ps

# View logs
docker compose logs -f
```

### Camera Mounting

- ✅ Allow air circulation around modules
- ✅ Avoid vibration-sensitive mounts
- ❌ Don't block ventilation grills
- ❌ Don't exceed max operating temps

- ✅ Deep sleep mode between measurements
- ✅ Brown-out detection enabled
- ✅ Power supply filtering capacitors
- ✅ Avoid 5V logic on 3.3V signals
- ✅ Use regulated power (>6V)

### Arduino Control Systems
- ✅ Use optocouplers for isolation
- ✅ Debounce signals via software
- ✅ Implement fail-safe defaults
- ✅ Monitor servo positions regularly
- ✅ Don't exceed 5V I2C voltage

- ✅ Calibrate depth cameras regularly
- ✅ Use LIDAR for indoor mapping

- ❌ Don't exceed 75% GPU load

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
ESP32 Camera IoT Implementation
================================

This module provides ESP32 camera integration for IoT vision nodes.
Supports multiple camera modules: OV2640, OV7675, OV8865, MIPI CSI.

Features:
- WiFi/BLE connectivity for MQTT pub/sub
- Deep sleep mode for power efficiency
- RGB, thermal, and depth camera support
- Built-in audio microphone arrays
- Sensor fusion (IMU, gyro, accelerometer)
- Power management (deep sleep, brown-out detection)

Usage:
    python camera_impl.py --camera ov2640 --resolution vga --bmi True
    python camera_impl.py --camera imx415 --resolution qhd --depth True
    python camera_impl.py --camera thermal --resolution vga --mqtt True
"""

import sys
import os
import time
import json
import logging
from typing import Optional, Dict, Any, List
from dataclasses import dataclass, asdict

# Import from parent package
from camera_py.camera_base import CameraNode, FrameData
import camera_esp32.camera_base as esp32_camera_base

# Configure logging
logging.basicConfig(
    level=logging.INFO,
    format='%(asctime)s - %(levelname)s - %(message)s',
    handlers=[
        logging.StreamHandler(sys.stdout),
        logging.FileHandler('/home/sabeiro/lav/src/blender_cv/logs/camera_esp32.log')
    ]
)
logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


@dataclass
class CameraConfig:
    """ESP32 Camera Configuration Class"""
    camera_id: str
    camera_type: str  # 'ov2640', 'ov7675', 'ov8865', 'imx415', 'thermal', 'depth'
    resolution: str   # 'vga', 'qhd', 'sd', 'hd', '4k'
    frame_rate: int
    audio_enabled: bool
    microphone_mode: str      # 'mono', 'stereo', 'array'
    mqtt_topic: str
    deep_sleep: bool
    wake_source: str        # 'touch', 'gpio_pin', 'motion'
    sleep_duration: int     # seconds
    brightness: int
    exposure_compensation: int
    white_balance: str      # 'auto', 'incandescent', 'tungsten', 'fluorescent', 'daylight'
    focus_distance: str     # 'near', 'far'
    flip_mirror_x: bool
    flif_mirror_y: bool
    sensor_power_mode: str   # 'normal', 'sleep', 'low_power', 'deep_sleep'
    
    def to_dict(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Convert config to dictionary for serialization"""
        return {
            'camera_id': self.camera_id,
            'camera_type': self.camera_type,
            'resolution': self.resolution,
            'frame_rate': self.frame_rate,
            'audio_enabled': self.audio_enabled,
            'microphone_mode': self.microphone_mode,
            'mqtt_topic': self.mqtt_topic,
            'deep_sleep': self.deep_sleep,
            'wake_source': self.wake_source,
            'sleep_duration': self.sleep_duration,
            'brightness': self.brightness,
            'exposure_compensation': self.exposure_compensation,
            'white_balance': self.white_balance,
            'focus_distance': self.focus_distance,
            'flip_horizontal': self.flip_mirror_x,
            'flip_vertical': self.flip_mirror_y,
            'sensor_power_mode': self.sensor_power_mode
        }


class ESP32Camera(esp32_camera_base.CameraNode):
    """
    ESP32 Camera IoT Node Class
    
    This class provides hardware-level ESP32 camera integration with
    support for multiple camera modules, WiFi/BLE connectivity,
    deep sleep mode, and MQTT pub/sub capabilities.
    
    Attributes:
        camera_id: Unique camera node identifier
        camera_type: Type of camera module
        frame_data: Captured frame data structure
    """
    
    # Supported camera modules with their specifications
    CAMERA_MODELS = {
        'ov2640': {
            'resolution': 'VGA (640x480)',
            'fps': '30',
            'interface': 'I2C bus'
        },
        'ov7675': {
            'resolution': 'VGA (640x480)',
            'fps': '30',
            'interface': 'I2C bus'
        },
        'ov8865': {
            'resolution': 'WVGA (800x480)',
            'fps': '30',
            'interface': 'I2C bus'
        },
        'imx415': {
            'resolution': 'QHD (1920x1080)',
            'fps': '60',
            'interface': 'MIPI CSI'
        },
        'thermal': {
            'resolution': 'VGA (640x480)',
            'fps': '25',
            'celsius': '10-70'
        },
        'depth': {
            'resolution': 'QVGA (320x240)',
            'fps': '30',
            'range': '0.2m to 1m'
        },
        'rgb_depth': {
            'resolution': 'QVGA (320x240)',
            'fps': '30',
            'range': '0.2m to 1m',
            'celsius': '10-50'
        }
    }
    
    def __init__(self, camera_id: str, camera_type: str, camera_config: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None):
        """
        Initialize ESP32 camera node
        
        Args:
            camera_id: Unique identifier for this camera node
            camera_type: Type of camera module (ov2640, imx415, etc.)
            camera_config: Optional dictionary with camera configuration
        """
        super().__init__(camera_id)
        
        # Default configuration with fallback values
        self.config: CameraConfig = CameraConfig(
            camera_id=camera_id,
            camera_type=camera_type,
            resolution='vga',
            frame_rate=30,
            audio_enabled=False,
            microphone_mode='mono',
            mqtt_topic=f'home/camera/{camera_id}',
            deep_sleep=False,
            wake_source='gpio_pin',
            sleep_duration=300,
            brightness=0,
            exposure_compensation=0,
            white_balance='auto',
            focus_distance='auto',
            flip_horizontal=False,
            flip_vertical=False,
            sensor_power_mode='normal'
        )
        
        # Override with provided config
        if camera_config:
            for key, value in camera_config.items():
                if hasattr(self.config, key):
                    setattr(self.config, key, value)
        
        logger.info(f"ESP32 camera node initialized: {self.config.to_dict()}")
    
    def initialize_camera(self) -> bool:
        """
        Initialize the ESP32 camera hardware
        
        Returns:
            bool: True if initialization successful
        
        Raises:
            RuntimeError: If camera initialization fails
        """
        logger.info(f"Initializing {self.camera_id} camera ({self.config.camera_type})")
        
        # Load camera firmware (stored in SPIFFS)
        try:
            with open(f'/home/sabeiro/camera_firmware/{self.config.camera_type}.bin', 'rb') as f:
                firmware = f.read()
        except FileNotFoundError:
            logger.warning(f"Firmware file not found, using default: {self.config.camera_type}")
            firmware = None
        
        # Initialize camera hardware
        try:
            self.camera = esp32_camera_base.ESP32CameraModule(
                camera_model=self.config.camera_type,
                resolution=self.config.resolution,
                frame_rate=self.config.frame_rate,
                audio_enabled=self.config.audio_enabled
            )
            
            # Configure camera settings
            self.camera.set_brightness(self.config.brightness)
            self.camera.set_exposure_compensation(self.config.exposure_compensation)
            self.camera.set_white_balance(self.config.white_balance)
            self.camera.set_focus_distance(self.config.focus_distance)
            
            # Enable audio if available
            if self.config.audio_enabled:
                self.camera.enable_microphone()
                self.camera.set_microphone_mode(self.config.microphone_mode)
            
            # Configure MQTT connection
            if self.config.mqtt_topic:
                self.mqtt_client.connect(
                    host='192.168.1.1',
                    port=1883,
                    topic=self.config.mqtt_topic
                )
            
            # Configure power management
            if self.config.deep_sleep:
                self.camera.enable_deep_sleep(
                    duration=self.config.sleep_duration,
                    wake_source=self.config.wake_source
                )
            
            logger.info(f"Camera {self.camera_id} initialized successfully")
            return True
            
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(f"Camera initialization failed: {e}")
            raise RuntimeError(f"Failed to initialize camera: {e}")
    
    def capture_frame(self) -> Optional[FrameData]:
        """
        Capture a single frame from the camera
        
        Returns:
            FrameData: Captured frame data with timestamp and metadata
            None: If capture failed or camera in sleep mode
        """
        # Check if camera is in deep sleep
        if self.config.deep_sleep and not self.camera.is_woken():
            logger.debug(f"Camera {self.camera_id} is in deep sleep, cannot capture")
            return None
        
        try:
            # Capture frame
            frame_bytes = self.camera.capture()
            
            if frame_bytes is None:
                logger.error(f"Frame capture failed for camera {self.camera_id}")
                return None
            
            # Create frame data
            frame_data = FrameData(
                camera_id=self.camera_id,
                timestamp=int(time.time() * 1000),
                width=self.config.width,
                height=self.config.height,
                bytes=frame_bytes,
                frame_type='rgb',  # 'rgb', 'thermal', 'depth', 'infrared'
                brightness=self.config.brightness,
                exposure_compensation=self.config.exposure_compmentation
            )
            
            # Send to MQTT if configured
            if self.config.mqtt_topic:
                self.mqtt_client.publish(
                    topic=self.config.mqtt_topic,
                    payload=json.dumps({
                        'camera_id': self.camera_id,
                        'timestamp': frame_data.timestamp,
                        'frame_type': self.config.frame_type,
                        'width': frame_data.width,
                        'height': frame_data.height
                    })
                )
            
            logger.debug(f"Frame captured: {frame_data.width}x{frame_data.height}")
            return frame_data
            
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(f"Frame capture error: {e}")
            return None
    
    def stream_frames(self, frame_rate: int = 30) -> bool:
        """
        Start continuous frame streaming
        
        Args:
            frame_rate: Frames per second
            
        Returns:
            bool: True if streaming started successfully
        """
        try:
            self.last_frame = self.capture_frame()
            
            if self.last_frame is None:
                logger.error("Cannot start streaming: frame capture failed")
                return False
            
            self.stream_running = True
            self.stream_fps = frame_rate
            
            # Start streaming loop
            import threading
            self._stream_thread = threading.Thread(target=self._stream_loop, args=(frame_rate,), daemon=True)
            self._stream_thread.start()
            
            logger.info(f"Streaming started: {frame_rate} FPS from camera {self.camera_id}")
            return True
            
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(f"Streaming failed: {e}")
            return False
    
    def stop_stream(self) -> bool:
        """Stop continuous frame streaming"""
        try:
            if hasattr(self, '_stream_thread'):
                self._stream_thread.join(timeout=5)
                self._stream_thread = None
            
            self.stream_running = False
            logger.info(f"Streaming stopped for camera {self.camera_id}")
            return True
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(f"Failed to stop streaming: {e}")
            return False
    
    def get_sensor_data(self) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
        """
        Get sensor data (IMU, temperature, etc.)
        
        Returns:
            dict: Sensor readings or None if unavailable
        """
        try:
            return {
                'temperature_celsius': self.camera.get_temperature(),
                'accelerometer_x': self.camera.get_accelerometer_x(),
                'accelerometer_y': self.camera.get_accelerometer_y(),
                'accelerometer_z': self.camera.get_accelerometer_z(),
                'gyroscope_x': self.camera.get_gyroscope_x(),
                'gyroscope_y': self.camera.get_gyroscope_y(),
                'gyroscope_z': self.camera.get_gyroscope_z(),
                'pressure_hpa': self.camera.get_pressure(),
                'humidity_pct': self.camera.get_humidity()
            }
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(f"Sensor data retrieval failed: {e}")
            return None
    
    def wakeup_camera(self) -> bool:
        """
        Wake camera from deep sleep
        
        Returns:
            bool: True if wake successful
        """
        try:
            self.camera.wake()
            time.sleep(1)  # Wait for initialization
            return True
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(f"Wake failed: {e}")
            return False
    
    def save_config(self, path: str) -> bool:
        """
        Save camera configuration to file
        
        Args:
            path: File path to save config
            
        Returns:
            bool: True if save successful
        """
        try:
            with open(path, 'w') as f:
                json.dump(self.config.to_dict(), f, indent=2)
            logger.info(f"Configuration saved to {path}")
            return True
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(f"Failed to save config to {path}: {e}")
            return False

# ESP32 IoT Camera Integration Project

## Overview

ESP32-based IoT cameras provide distributed sensing edge nodes for multi-camera systems, offering Wi-Fi/BLE connectivity, MQTT pub/sub capabilities, deep sleep mode, and support for multiple camera modules (RGB, thermal, depth).

---

## Architecture

## Software Architecture

### Camera Types

**1. RGB Camera (Color Imaging)**

**2. Thermal Sensor**
- Camera: Infrared (MLX90614, TCS34725)
- Use Cases: Heat signature, temperature monitoring

**3. Depth Camera**

- Use Cases: Gesture control, proximity, obstacle avoidance
- Features: Point cloud output, 3D mapping

def tone_mapping(luminance_map):
    """Adaptive tone mapping for HDR images"""
    from scipy.ndimage import gaussian_filter
    
    # Calculate exposure brackets
    short_exp = 0.7 * luminance_map
    mid_exp = 1.0 * luminance_map
    long_exp = 1.3 * luminance_map
    
    # Merge exposures with adaptive weighting

## Troubleshooting

### Common Issues

**Problem: Camera not detected**
- Check I2C bus address: `i2cdetect -y -r /dev/i2c-<bus>`
- Verify camera power: `lsusb` (for USB cameras)
- Check camera firmware: `esptool.py flash_start`

**Problem: Low frame rate**
- Reduce resolution: `--resolution vga`
- Enable deep sleep to save power
- Check MQTT connection bandwidth

**Problem: Sensor fusion drift**
- Recalibrate IMU: `python calibrate_imu.py`
- Check for magnetic interference
- Verify Kalman filter parameters

# System Configuration

## Environment
- **OS:** Ubuntu 26.04 LTS
- **Architecture:** x86-64 / ARM64 (Jetson Orin)
- **GPU:** NVIDIA RTX 5060 (8GB VRAM) / Jetson Orin Nano (10 TOPS)
- **RAM:** 32GB (Recommended: 64GB for high-throughput)
- **Storage:** 500GB+ NVMe SSD (Recommended: 1TB with RAID0)
- **Power:** 220W+ continuous (with GPU)
- **Network:** Gigabit Ethernet / Wi-Fi 6

## Hardware Support

### Edge Nodes
- Jetson Orin Nano (4GB RAM, 12 TOPS NPU)
- Jetson Orin NX (16GB RAM, 216 TOPS)
- NVIDIA RTX 5060 (8GB GDDR6)
- RTX 4070/4080 for high-throughput
- Coral TPU for inference acceleration

### Supported Camera Modules
- OV2640 (VGA, 30 FPS)
- IMX219 (HD, 30 FPS)
- IMX477 (QHD, 60 FPS)
- Thermal sensors (MLX90614)
- Depth cameras (ToF, LIAR)
- RGB+Depth fusion

### Sensors
- IMU (accelerometer, gyroscope)
- Barometric pressure
- Temperature & humidity
- Microphone array (8-channel)
- GPS/Geolocation
- LiDAR (optional)

---

## Security Policies

### Network Access
```
# External network access
┌─────────┐──────┬─────────────┐
│ Internal│───●──┤ External    │
│   Net   │  Yes │    Blocked  │
└─────────┘──────┴─────────────┘
```

- Local development only (127.0.0.1)
- No external network access in containers
- Port forwarding restricted
- No outbound connections except to trusted services
- Rate limiting on external endpoints

### File Permissions
```bash
# Directory permissions
data/           drwxr-xr-x     755
logs/           drwxr-xr-x     700
config/         drwxr-xrw-     750
models/         drwxr-x---     750
sensitive/      drwxr-----     700

# File permissions
*.py           644
*.pyc          640
*.conf         600
*.key          600
*.pem          600

# Sensitive data
credentials/    drwx------     700
private_keys/   drwx------     700
```

### Container Permissions
- No sudo execution from containers
- Read-only file permissions on shared volumes
- Drop capabilities: `--cap-drop=ALL`
- No privileged containers
- Seccomp profile: `default`
- AppArmor profile: `docker-default`

---

## Deployment Modes

### A) Development Mode

```bash
# Enable debug logging
LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG

# Permissive security
MODE=development
ALLOW_INsecure=1

# Resource limits relaxed
MAX_MEMORY=8GB
MAX_CPU=80%
```

**Features:**
- All MCP tools enabled
- Unlimited context window
- Full system access
- Debug mode enabled
- No rate limiting

### B) Production Mode

```bash
# Production settings
LOG_LEVEL=INFO
MODE=production

# Resource restrictions
MAX_MEMORY=4GB
MAX_CPU=90%
MAX_CONCURRENT=4

# Security hardening
ENCRYPT_SECRETS=1
RATE_LIMIT=100/s
```

**Features:**
- Production-hardened security
- Rate limiting
- Resource capping
- Audit logging
- Health checks

### C) Edge Mode

```bash
# Edge deployment
MODE=edge
LOW_POWER_MODE=1
DEEP_SLEEP_ENABLED=1

# Wake triggers
WAKE_ON_MOTION=1
WAKE_ON_GPIO=1
WAKE_ON_WIFI=1
```

**Features:**
- Deep sleep mode
- Low-power operation
- Local processing only
- Minimal network use
- Battery optimization

---

## Ollama Configuration

### Model Constraints

```yaml
# Max concurrent requests
max_concurrent_requests: 2
context_window: 8192  # tokens
keep_alive: 10m  # minutes
model_memory_limit: 8GB

# Model caching
model_cache_size: 10GB
auto_download: true
prune_old_models: true

# Response time
max_response_time_ms: 30000
min_throughput_rpm: 5
```

### Context Management

```yaml
# Context window
max_tokens: 8192
default_context: 2048
compression: 0.65

# Memory optimization
memory_budget: 16GB
quantization: fp16
keep_alive_window: 110m
```

### Request Queue

```yaml
queue_max_size: 100
queue_timeout_ms: 30000
fallback_model: ""
priority_queue: true
```

---

## Resource Monitoring

### Performance Metrics

```python
# CPU usage
cpu_current: < 90%
cpu_average: < 70%
cpu_spike_threshold: > 100%

# Memory usage
memory_used: < 4GB
memory_average: < 2.5GB
memory_swap: 0

# Disk I/O
read_ops: < 500/s
write_ops: < 100/s
disk_utilization: < 80%

# Network throughput
upload_rate: < 100MB/s
download_rate: < 200MB/s
latency_p99: < 50ms
```

### Alert Thresholds

```bash
# Warning thresholds
LOGGING_MEMORY_WARNING=80%
LOGGING_CPU_WARNING=80%
LOGGING_DISK_WARNING=85%
LOGGING_NETWORK_WARNING=90%

# Critical thresholds
ALERT_MEMORY_CRITICAL=95%
ALERT_CPU_CRITICAL=95%
ALERT_DISK_CRITICAL=95%
ALERT_NETWORK_CRITICAL=95%
```

---

## MCP Server Configuration

### Tool Definitions

```yaml
# Code tools
code-read:
  description: Read source files and logs
  capabilities: [read, analyze]
  scope: [src/, logs/, config/]

code-ask:
  description: Analyze code without execution
  capabilities: [syntax, logic]
  max_tokens: 8192

code-run:
  description: Execute code with restrictions
  capabilities: [execute, output]
  restrictions: [no_network, safe_only]

  memory_limit_mb: 512

max_concurrent_tools: 4
tool_timeout_ms: 30000
request_validation: true
```

### Security Model

```yaml
# Read-only tools
read_only:
  tools: [code-read, code-ask]
  scope: [/src/, /logs/, /data/]

  tools: [code-run]
  restrictions: [write_file:/logs/, write_file:/data/]

admin_tools:
  tools: []
  scope: [/]
  restrictions: []
```

---

## Network Configuration

### Local Network

```yaml
host: 127.0.0.1
port_ollama: 11434
port_mcp: 18789
port_api: 8000

# Bind address
bind_address: 0.0.0.0
external_access: true
```

### External Access

```yaml
# Production mode
external_network: false

# Allow-listed IPs (optional)
allow_ips: []  # Empty = no access

# Rate limiting
rate_limit_requests: 100/s
rate_limit_window: 60s
```

---

### CPU Management

```yaml
# Per-process limits
max_cpu_percent: 90
cpu_affinity: []
cpu_isolation: true

# Process controls
nice_level: 19
pdeath_signal: 9
oom_score_adj: -500
```

### Memory Management

```yaml
# Memory limits

cache_memory_max: 2GB
heap_memory_max: 1.5GB

# Swapping policy
memory_swap_enabled: false
memory_overcommit: false
```

```yaml

max_connections: 300

queue_depth: 100
queue_timeout: 30s
backlog_max: 4
```

    scipy>=1.11.0 \

    pillow>=10.0.0 \
    uvicorn>=0.23.0 \
    fastapi>=0.100.0
```

```yaml

# Jetson CV - Digital Twin Prototype for On-Prem Deployment

**Prototype project** for on-premises digital twin systems using NVIDIA Jetson hardware, local AI inference, and FEM/physics simulations. **No cloud providers** - fully on-prem solution using local Ollama instances and Jetson Orin Nano for edge computing.

## Architecture

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                Digital Twin Ecosystem                      │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  ┌─────────────┐    ┌─────────────┐    ┌─────────────┐   │
│  │   Blender   │    │   Visual    │    │   3D        │   │
│  │  Integration│    │   Graphics  │    │             │   │
│  └─────────────┘    └─────────────┘    └─────────────┘   │
│                          │        │            │           │
│  ┌──────────────────────┼─────────┼────────┐  │           │
│  │  Computer Vision     │ FEM      │ Physics│  │           │
│  │  Pose Est.          │ Solver   │ Sim.   │  │           │
│  │  Object Det.        │ Heat     │ CFD    │  │           │
│  └─────────────────────┼─────────┴────────┘  │           │
│                        │                    │           │
│  ┌─────────────────────▼──────────────────▼───┐          │
│  │         Real-World Sensors (IoT)           │          │
│  │  ┌──────────┐ ┌──────────┐ ┌────────────┐ │          │
│  │  │ Camera   │ │ IoT      │ │ OPC-UA     │ │          │
│  │  │ Sensor   │ │ Stream   │ │ MQTT       │ │          │
│  │  └──────────┘ └──────────┘ └────────────┘ │          │
│  └────────────────────────────────────────────┘          │
│                          │                                │
│  ┌───────────────────────▼───────────────────────────────┐│
│  │    Knowledge Graphs │ Optimization Energy              ││
│  │    GraphDB/RDF      │ Engine                           ││
│  └─────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────────┘│
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Project Structure

```
blender_cv/
├── README.md                      # This file - Project overview
├── README.org                     # Org mode documentation
├── sys_sync.sh                    # System synchronization script
├── pi_config/                     # MCP agent configuration
│   ├── SKILLS.md                  # Available skills/agents
│   ├── AGENTS.md                  # MCP agent roles
│   ├── SYSTEM.md                  # Core system policies
│   └── SYSTEM_APPEND.md           # Project-specific overrides
├── camera_esp32/                  # ESP32-based IoT cameras
├── camera_py/                     # Python camera implementations
├── camera/                        # Runtime application (TensorRT)
├── controller_apk/                # Android controller applications
├── controller_arduino/            # Arduino-based controllers
├── controller_js/                 # JavaScript controllers
├── controller_m5stack/            # M5Stack hardware integration
├── controller_pico/               # Raspberry Pi Pico integration
├── controller_c/                  # C-based controller implementations
├── heat_fem/                      # FEM thermal analysis (DOLPHIN/FEniCS)
├── manage_jetson/                 # Jetson deployment management
├── media/                         # Output images/videos
├── model/                         # Saved AI models (.onnx, .pt, .engine)
├── phys_opt/                      # Physics optimization engines
├── pose_estimate_of/              # OpenFrameworks C++ models
├── pose_estimate_py/              # PyTorch/Ultralytics models
└── video_to_3d/                   # Video reconstruction pipelines
```

## Hardware Requirements


## Hardware Stack Architecture
- **Storage:** 32GB SSD (expandable to 1TB+ for media)


## Hardware Stack Architecture

### Core Edge Computing (Primary Targets)
- **NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano** (4GB/8GB RAM) - Primary deployment target
  - JetPack 6.x with TensorRT acceleration
  - Real-time inference (≤100ms latency)
  - Container isolation for multiple services

- **NVIDIA RTX 5060** (desktop) - Alternative for offline rendering
  - High-throughput batch processing
  - 3D scene reconstruction
  - FEM simulation visualization

### Edge IoT Devices (Distributed Sensing)
- **ESP32** (IoT Cameras, MQTT Broker Nodes)
  - WiFi/BLE enabled
  - Deep sleep mode for power efficiency
  - RGB, thermal, depth cameras
  - MQTT pub/sub capabilities
  - Microphone arrays for audio
  - Accelerometer + gyroscope sensors
  - Custom PCB mounting options

- **Arduino Uno R4** (Controller Applications)
  - WiFi & BLE modules
  - Real-time control logic
  - I2C/SPI sensors integration
  - Servo motor drivers
  - ADC for analog signals
  - CAN bus support

- **Raspberry Pi Zero W/2 W** (Lightweight Edge Nodes)
  - Pi Camera Module support
  - CSI camera interfaces
  - LoRaWAN expansion
  - GPIO sensor arrays
  - Lightweight inference (quantized models)

- **Raspberry Pi Pico/Pico 2** (Microcontroller Edge)
  - RP2040 dual-core ARM
  - 125MHz-133MHz CPU
  - PWM control (motors, servos)
  - I2C/SPI sensor buses
  - BLE/UART communication
  - Deep sleep support

- **Raspberry Pi 4/5** (Workstation Deployment)
  - Full desktop applications
  - Multiple CSI camera inputs
  - FEM simulation rendering
  - Docker container hosting
  - High-bandwidth SSD storage

- **M5Stack** (Modular Sensors Platform)
  - ESP32-WROOM + ATwin module
  - AI Kit with Coral TPU
  - LIDAR + cameras
  - Depth cameras (ToF)
  - Accelerometer + gyroscope
  - Microphone array
  - LoRa + WiFi + BLE

### Camera Modules Supported
- **CSI Cameras** (Native Jetson)
  - IMX219 (standard RGB)
  - IMX477 (global shutter)
  - IMX335 (wide angle)
  - IMX415 (depth/3D)
  - RGB + IR + Thermal multi-sensor
  - 4K @ 60fps capable

- **USB Cameras** (Fallback/Development)
  - Logitech C920/C930
  - Intel RealSense D435
  - Microsoft Kinect (legacy)
  - Micro USB cameras

- **ESP32 Cameras** (IoT Vision Nodes)
  - OV2640 (VGA, low cost)
  - OV7670 + V2
  - OV8865 (WVGA, color)
  - MIPI interface options

- **M5Stack Cameras** (Depth Sensing)
  - TOF depth camera
  - RGB depth array
  - 3D point cloud output

### Camera Integration Features
- **Multi-camera fusion** - Sensor data merging
- **Camera calibration** - Intrinsics/Extrinsics
- **Color correction** - White balance
- **HDR processing** - Tone mapping
- **Exposure control** - Auto/manual
- **Focus distance** - Near/far focus
- **Frame rate control** - FPS throttling
- **Buffer management** - Circular queues

### Hardware Communication Interfaces

- **I2C** - Sensor data reading (IMU, temp, pressure)
- **SPI** - Camera modules, display panels
- **UART** - Serial console, BLE dongles
- **GPIO** - Digital I/O, PWM control
- **CAN Bus** - Automotive-grade control
- **Ethernet** - High-bandwidth networking
- **WiFi/BLE** - Wireless sensor networks
- **LoRa** - Low power long-range

### Resource Requirements by Deployment

| Device | RAM | GPU | CPU | Storage |
|--------|-----|-----|-----|---------|
| Jetson Orin | 8GB | 120 TOPS | 4x A76AE | NVMe SSD |
| RTX 5060 | 16GB+ | 6GB GDDR6 | 6-core CPU | |
| Raspberry Pi | 4GB | CPU-only | Quad-core | SD/NVMe |
| ESP32 | 520KB | N/A | Tenspeed | Flash |
| Arduino | 2KB | N/A | N/A | Flash |
| M5Stack | 520KB | Coral TPU | 4GB eMMC | |

### Storage Recommendations
- **NVMe SSD** - Primary models/data (32GB+ minimum)
- **SD Card** - Backup for Pi devices (16GB+ Class 10)
- **USB Flash** - Portable configuration files
- **HDD** - Archival media (8TB+ recommended)

---

## Hardware Requirements

### Minimum Resources
- **Jetson:** 8GB RAM, JetPack 6.x
- **PC Workstation:** 16GB RAM, 4GB+ GPU
- **Edge Nodes:** 4GB+ (Raspberry Pi/Zero)
- **MCU Nodes:** 520KB+ (ESP32/Pico)

---

---

## Core Components

### 1. Computer Vision Pipeline (`camera_py/`, `camera/`)

Real-time pose estimation using TensorRT-accelerated models:

- **pose_estimate_py/** - PyTorch/Ultralytics training & export
  - Train custom pose models with YOLO11n-pose
  - Export to ONNX for TensorRT conversion
  - Batch processing with queue management

- **pose_estimate_of/** - OpenFrameworks C++ for high-performance inference
  - ONNX runtime integration
  - Low-latency deployment

- **model/** - Model artifacts storage:
  - `.pt` - PyTorch models (training)
  - `.onnx` - ONNX Intermediate format
  - `.engine` - TensorRT optimized engines

**Features:**
- CSI camera support (IMX219, RGB, thermal)
- Real-time inference (≤100ms latency)
- Zoom, pan, flip controls
- Photo/video capture
- Histogram and vectorscope displays

### 2. Finite Element Analysis (`heat_fem/`)

Thermal and structural simulations using FEniCSx/DOLPHIN:

- **FEM Mesh** - Adaptive mesh refinement
- **Thermal Analysis** - Heat transfer, conduction, radiation
- **Structural** - Stress, strain, deformation
- **Optimization** - Topology optimization for lightweight designs

**Features:**
- HDF5 output for large datasets
- 30-minute solver timeout
- Mesh quality validation
- Parallel computation (8 cores max)

### 3. Physics Optimization (`phys_opt/`)

Constraint-based optimization engines:

- **Pyomo** - Mathematical modeling
- **IPOPT** - Interior-point optimization
- **Result caching** - 24-hour cache
- **Multi-physics** - Thermal + structural + fluid

### 4. Visualization & 3D (`blender_cv/`, `video_to_3d/`)

3D modeling and rendering:

- **Blender integration** - 3D scene assembly
- **ONNX models** - Direct export to 3D
- **WebGL** - Web-based 3D viewers
- **Export formats** - .obj, .fbx, .glb

### 5. IoT & Sensor Integration

Real-world data ingestion:

- **MQTT** - MQTT broker for sensor pub/sub
- **OPC-UA** - Industrial device integration
- **CoAP** - Lightweight MQTT alternative
- **Sensor fusion** - Multi-sensor data merging
- **Data streams** - High-frequency telemetry

### 6. Edge Computing & Deployment

On-prem deployment capabilities:

- **JetPack 6.x** - NVIDIA accelerated runtime
- **TensorRT** - GPU-accelerated inference
- **ONNX Runtime** - CPU GPU interoperability
- **Model optimization** - Quantization, pruning for edge
- **Docker/Kubernetes** - Container orchestration
- **sys_sync.sh** - System synchronization script

---

## On-Prem Architecture

### Network Design
```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐
│    ON-PREM ONLY - No Cloud Connection    │
├──────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  ┌─────────────┐                        │
│  │ Jetson      │                        │
│  │ Orin Nano   │ ─────────────────────► │
│  │ (Edge Node) │  Real-time Inference   │
│  └─────────────┘                        │
├──────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  ┌─────────────┐                        │
│  │ Ollama      │                        │
│  │ Local       │                        │
│  │ Instance    │                        │
│  └─────────────┘                        │
├──────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  ┌─────────────┐                        │
│  │ GraphDB     │                        │
│  │ Knowledge   │                        │
│  └─────────────┘                        │
├──────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  ┌─────────────┐                        │
│  │ MQTT Broker │                        │
│  │ (RabbitMQ)  │                        │
│  └─────────────┘                        │
├──────────────────────────────────────────│
│  ┌─────────────┐                        │
│  │ NVMe SSD    │                        │
│  │ Storage     │                        │
│  └─────────────┘                        │
└──────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Security
- **No SSH** from untrusted networks
- **Container isolation** for all services
- **Read-only** file permissions on shared volumes
- **Local LLM** only (Ollama - no API keys)
- **No external** database connections

---

## Digital Twin Capabilities

### What's Included
- **Visual Twin** - 3D models from Blender + pose estimation
- **Physical Twin** - FEM + physics simulations + multi-physics
- **Sensing Twin** - IoT integration, real-time data streams
- **Intelligent Twin** - ML models, knowledge graphs, predictive analytics
- **Optimized Twin** - Energy modeling, resource allocation
- **Connected Twin** - MQTT, OPC-UA, standard protocols

### Skills Available
See `pi_config/SKILLS.md` for complete skill definitions:
- FEM/FEniCS → Structural/mechanical analysis
- Optimization → Energy/resource optimization
- Vision → Real-time object tracking
- Knowledge graph → Component relationships
- IoT → MQTT, OPC-UA integration
- Time series → Historical analysis
- Edge computing → On-device inference

---

## Quick Start

### 1. Environment Setup

```bash
# Load CUDA environment
export CUDA_HOME=/usr/local/cuda
export PATH=$CUDA_HOME/bin:$PATH
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=$CUDA_HOME/lib64:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH
export CPATH=$CUDA_HOME/include:$CPATH

source ~/.bashrc
```

### 2. Install Dependencies

```bash
# System packages
sudo apt install python3-opencv python3-numpy

# Python packages
cd camera
pip install -r requirements.txt

# Configure camera (CSI)
sudo /opt/nvidia/jetson-io/jetson-io.py
```

### 3. Build Models

```bash
# Train pose model
cd pose_estimate_py
python train.py

# Export to ONNX
model.export(format='onnx')
mv model.onnx ../model/

# Create TensorRT engine
cd ../camera
python build_engine.py
```

### 4. Run Application

```bash
cd camera
python -m camera.camera_controller

# Or use Docker
docker compose up -d
```

### 5. Deploy Digital Twin

```bash
# Start all services
docker compose up -d

# Check status
docker compose ps

# View logs
docker compose logs -f
```

---

## Skills & Agents Configuration

The pi_config/ directory contains MCP agent configurations:
- **SKILLS.md** - All available skills for digital twin operations
- **AGENTS.md** - Agent roles and responsibilities
- **SYSTEM.md** - Core system policies and constraints
- **SYSTEM_APPEND.md** - Project-specific overrides

See [SKILLS.md](mcp_server/ollama/pi_config/SKILLS.md) for complete skill catalog.

## Testing & Quality

### Code Quality
- **Unit tests ≥70%** - Coverage requirement
- **Static analysis** - pylint, black, flake8
- **Lint** - No production code without testing
- **Documentation** - Type hints, docstrings

### CI/CD (Local Only)

## Development Guidelines

### Code Style
- **Python** - PEP8, type hints, docstrings
- **C++** - Modern C++17/20, RAII principles
- **Blender** - bpy, operators, operators only

### Documentation
- **Markdown** - Technical documentation
- **Org mode** - Research notes (README.org)
- **API docs** - Sphinx for Python modules

### Testing
- **Unit tests** - Test individual components
- **Integration tests** - MCP tool workflows
- **End-to-end** - Full digital twin scenarios
- **Performance** - Inference latency checks

---

## Deployment Checklists

### Pre-Deployment
- ✅ All dependencies installed
- ✅ Models trained and exported to ONNX
- ✅ Docker containers built
- ✅ Test data generated
- ✅ Logs configured for JSON output

### Post-Deployment
- ✅ Services running (docker compose ps)
- ✅ Logs healthy (docker compose logs | grep ERROR)
- ✅ Models loaded (ollama list)
- ✅ Camera feed active
- ✅ MQTT broker responding

---

## Support & Resources

### Documentation
- **README.org** - Org mode with math/formulas
- **SKILLS.md** - Full skill catalog
- **AGENTS.md** - MCP agent roles
- **SYSTEM.md** - System policies

### External References
- **NVIDIA Jetson** - https://developer.nvidia.com/jetson
- **TensorRT** - https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/tensorrt/
- **ONNX** - https://onnx.ai/
- **Blender** - https://www.blender.org/
- **FEniCSx** - https://fems.readthedocs.io/
- **DOLPHIN** - https://fems.readthedocs.io/

---

## Contributing

1. Fork this prototype repository
2. Create feature branches
3. Add tests for new functionality
4. Update SKILLS.md for new capabilities
5. Submit pull request with documentation

### Code Review Checklist
- [ ] Lint passes (pylint, black, flake8)
- [ ] Unit tests added
- [ ] Code coverage ≥70%
- [ ] Documentation updated
- [ ] SKILLS.md updated (if new skill)

---

## License

MIT License - Feel free to use for on-prem digital twin projects

---

## Notes

- This is a **prototype** for on-prem digital twin systems
- **No cloud** - All processing local to Jetson/PC
- **Ollama** - Local LLM for agent assistance
- **On-prem only** - No external services or APIs
- **Edge-first** - Jetson Orin Nano for deployment

## Project Highlights

- ✅ **Fully on-prem** - No cloud dependencies
- ✅ **Local LLM** - Ollama for agent interactions
- ✅ **Edge computing** - Jetson Orin Nano deployment
- ✅ **Digital twin stack** - Complete FEM + vision + IoT
- ✅ **Standard protocols** - MQTT, OPC-UA, DTCL
- ✅ **No external dependencies** - Self-contained system

# Jetson CV - Digital Twin Prototype for On-Prem Deployment

**Prototype project** for on-premises digital twin systems using NVIDIA Jetson hardware, local AI inference, and FEM/physics simulations. **No cloud providers** - fully on-prem solution using local Ollama instances and Jetson Orin Nano for edge computing.

## Architecture

## Hardware Requirements


## Hardware Stack Architecture
- **Storage:** 32GB SSD (expandable to 1TB+ for media)


## Hardware Stack Architecture

### Core Edge Computing (Primary Targets)
- **NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano** (4GB/8GB RAM) - Primary deployment target
  - JetPack 6.x with TensorRT acceleration
  - Real-time inference (≤100ms latency)
  - Container isolation for multiple services

- **NVIDIA RTX 5060** (desktop) - Alternative for offline rendering
  - High-throughput batch processing
  - 3D scene reconstruction
  - FEM simulation visualization

### Edge IoT Devices (Distributed Sensing)
- **ESP32** (IoT Cameras, MQTT Broker Nodes)
  - WiFi/BLE enabled
  - Deep sleep mode for power efficiency
  - RGB, thermal, depth cameras
  - MQTT pub/sub capabilities
  - Microphone arrays for audio
  - Accelerometer + gyroscope sensors
  - Custom PCB mounting options

- **Arduino Uno R4** (Controller Applications)
  - WiFi & BLE modules
  - Real-time control logic
  - I2C/SPI sensors integration
  - Servo motor drivers
  - ADC for analog signals
  - CAN bus support

- **Raspberry Pi Zero W/2 W** (Lightweight Edge Nodes)
  - Pi Camera Module support
  - CSI camera interfaces
  - LoRaWAN expansion
  - GPIO sensor arrays
  - Lightweight inference (quantized models)

- **Raspberry Pi Pico/Pico 2** (Microcontroller Edge)
  - RP2040 dual-core ARM
  - 125MHz-133MHz CPU
  - PWM control (motors, servos)
  - I2C/SPI sensor buses
  - BLE/UART communication
  - Deep sleep support

- **Raspberry Pi 4/5** (Workstation Deployment)
  - Full desktop applications
  - Multiple CSI camera inputs
  - FEM simulation rendering
  - Docker container hosting
  - High-bandwidth SSD storage

- **M5Stack** (Modular Sensors Platform)
  - ESP32-WROOM + ATwin module
  - AI Kit with Coral TPU
  - LIDAR + cameras
  - Depth cameras (ToF)
  - Accelerometer + gyroscope
  - Microphone array
  - LoRa + WiFi + BLE

### Camera Modules Supported
- **CSI Cameras** (Native Jetson)
  - IMX219 (standard RGB)
  - IMX477 (global shutter)
  - IMX335 (wide angle)
  - IMX415 (depth/3D)
  - RGB + IR + Thermal multi-sensor
  - 4K @ 60fps capable

- **USB Cameras** (Fallback/Development)
  - Logitech C920/C930
  - Intel RealSense D435
  - Microsoft Kinect (legacy)
  - Micro USB cameras

- **ESP32 Cameras** (IoT Vision Nodes)
  - OV2640 (VGA, low cost)
  - OV7670 + V2
  - OV8865 (WVGA, color)
  - MIPI interface options

- **M5Stack Cameras** (Depth Sensing)
  - TOF depth camera
  - RGB depth array
  - 3D point cloud output

### Camera Integration Features
- **Multi-camera fusion** - Sensor data merging
- **Camera calibration** - Intrinsics/Extrinsics
- **Color correction** - White balance
- **HDR processing** - Tone mapping
- **Exposure control** - Auto/manual
- **Focus distance** - Near/far focus
- **Frame rate control** - FPS throttling
- **Buffer management** - Circular queues

### Hardware Communication Interfaces

- **I2C** - Sensor data reading (IMU, temp, pressure)
- **SPI** - Camera modules, display panels
- **UART** - Serial console, BLE dongles
- **GPIO** - Digital I/O, PWM control
- **CAN Bus** - Automotive-grade control
- **Ethernet** - High-bandwidth networking
- **WiFi/BLE** - Wireless sensor networks
- **LoRa** - Low power long-range

### Resource Requirements by Deployment

| Device | RAM | GPU | CPU | Storage |
|--------|-----|-----|-----|---------|
| Jetson Orin | 8GB | 120 TOPS | 4x A76AE | NVMe SSD |
| RTX 5060 | 16GB+ | 6GB GDDR6 | 6-core CPU | |
| Raspberry Pi | 4GB | CPU-only | Quad-core | SD/NVMe |
| ESP32 | 520KB | N/A | Tenspeed | Flash |
| Arduino | 2KB | N/A | N/A | Flash |
| M5Stack | 520KB | Coral TPU | 4GB eMMC | |

### Storage Recommendations
- **NVMe SSD** - Primary models/data (32GB+ minimum)
- **SD Card** - Backup for Pi devices (16GB+ Class 10)
- **USB Flash** - Portable configuration files
- **HDD** - Archival media (8TB+ recommended)

---

## Hardware Requirements

### Minimum Resources
- **Jetson:** 8GB RAM, JetPack 6.x
- **PC Workstation:** 16GB RAM, 4GB+ GPU
- **Edge Nodes:** 4GB+ (Raspberry Pi/Zero)
- **MCU Nodes:** 520KB+ (ESP32/Pico)

---

---

## Core Components

### 1. Computer Vision Pipeline (`camera_py/`, `camera/`)

Real-time pose estimation using TensorRT-accelerated models:

- **pose_estimate_py/** - PyTorch/Ultralytics training & export
  - Train custom pose models with YOLO11n-pose
  - Export to ONNX for TensorRT conversion
  - Batch processing with queue management

- **pose_estimate_of/** - OpenFrameworks C++ for high-performance inference
  - ONNX runtime integration
  - Low-latency deployment

- **model/** - Model artifacts storage:
  - `.pt` - PyTorch models (training)
  - `.onnx` - ONNX Intermediate format
  - `.engine` - TensorRT optimized engines

**Features:**
- CSI camera support (IMX219, RGB, thermal)
- Real-time inference (≤100ms latency)
- Zoom, pan, flip controls
- Photo/video capture
- Histogram and vectorscope displays

### 2. Finite Element Analysis (`heat_fem/`)

Thermal and structural simulations using FEniCSx/DOLPHIN:

- **FEM Mesh** - Adaptive mesh refinement
- **Thermal Analysis** - Heat transfer, conduction, radiation
- **Structural** - Stress, strain, deformation
- **Optimization** - Topology optimization for lightweight designs

**Features:**
- HDF5 output for large datasets
- 30-minute solver timeout
- Mesh quality validation
- Parallel computation (8 cores max)

### 3. Physics Optimization (`phys_opt/`)

Constraint-based optimization engines:

- **Pyomo** - Mathematical modeling
- **IPOPT** - Interior-point optimization
- **Result caching** - 24-hour cache
- **Multi-physics** - Thermal + structural + fluid

### 4. Visualization & 3D (`blender_cv/`, `video_to_3d/`)

3D modeling and rendering:

- **Blender integration** - 3D scene assembly
- **ONNX models** - Direct export to 3D
- **WebGL** - Web-based 3D viewers
- **Export formats** - .obj, .fbx, .glb

### 5. IoT & Sensor Integration

Real-world data ingestion:

- **MQTT** - MQTT broker for sensor pub/sub
- **OPC-UA** - Industrial device integration
- **CoAP** - Lightweight MQTT alternative
- **Sensor fusion** - Multi-sensor data merging
- **Data streams** - High-frequency telemetry

### 6. Edge Computing & Deployment

On-prem deployment capabilities:

- **JetPack 6.x** - NVIDIA accelerated runtime
- **TensorRT** - GPU-accelerated inference
- **ONNX Runtime** - CPU GPU interoperability
- **Model optimization** - Quantization, pruning for edge
- **Docker/Kubernetes** - Container orchestration
- **sys_sync.sh** - System synchronization script

---

### Security
- **No SSH** from untrusted networks
- **Container isolation** for all services
- **Read-only** file permissions on shared volumes
- **Local LLM** only (Ollama - no API keys)
- **No external** database connections

---

## Digital Twin Capabilities

### What's Included
- **Visual Twin** - 3D models from Blender + pose estimation
- **Physical Twin** - FEM + physics simulations + multi-physics
- **Sensing Twin** - IoT integration, real-time data streams
- **Intelligent Twin** - ML models, knowledge graphs, predictive analytics
- **Optimized Twin** - Energy modeling, resource allocation
- **Connected Twin** - MQTT, OPC-UA, standard protocols

### Skills Available
See `pi_config/SKILLS.md` for complete skill definitions:
- FEM/FEniCS → Structural/mechanical analysis
- Optimization → Energy/resource optimization
- Vision → Real-time object tracking
- Knowledge graph → Component relationships
- IoT → MQTT, OPC-UA integration
- Time series → Historical analysis
- Edge computing → On-device inference

## Quick Start

### 1. Environment Setup

```bash
# Load CUDA environment
export CUDA_HOME=/usr/local/cuda
export PATH=$CUDA_HOME/bin:$PATH
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=$CUDA_HOME/lib64:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH
export CPATH=$CUDA_HOME/include:$CPATH

source ~/.bashrc
```

### 2. Install Dependencies

```bash
# System packages
sudo apt install python3-opencv python3-numpy

# Python packages
cd camera
pip install -r requirements.txt

# Configure camera (CSI)
sudo /opt/nvidia/jetson-io/jetson-io.py
```

### 3. Build Models

```bash
# Train pose model
cd pose_estimate_py
python train.py

# Export to ONNX
model.export(format='onnx')
mv model.onnx ../model/

# Create TensorRT engine
cd ../camera
python build_engine.py
```

### 4. Run Application

```bash
cd camera
python -m camera.camera_controller

# Or use Docker
docker compose up -d
```

### 5. Deploy Digital Twin

```bash
# Start all services
docker compose up -d

# Check status
docker compose ps

# View logs
docker compose logs -f
```

# Jetson CV - Digital Twin Prototype for On-Prem Deployment

**Prototype project** for on-premises digital twin systems using NVIDIA Jetson hardware, local AI inference, and FEM/physics simulations. **No cloud providers** - fully on-prem solution using local Ollama instances and Jetson Orin Nano for edge computing.

## Architecture

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                Digital Twin Ecosystem                      │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  ┌─────────────┐    ┌─────────────┐    ┌─────────────┐   │
│  │   Blender   │    │   Visual    │    │   3D        │   │
│  │  Integration│    │   Graphics  │    │             │   │
│  └─────────────┘    └─────────────┘    └─────────────┘   │
│                          │        │            │           │
│  ┌──────────────────────┼─────────┼────────┐  │           │
│  │  Computer Vision     │ FEM      │ Physics│  │           │
│  │  Pose Est.          │ Solver   │ Sim.   │  │           │
│  │  Object Det.        │ Heat     │ CFD    │  │           │
│  └─────────────────────┼─────────┴────────┘  │           │
│                        │                    │           │
│  ┌─────────────────────▼──────────────────▼───┐          │
│  │         Real-World Sensors (IoT)           │          │
│  │  ┌──────────┐ ┌──────────┐ ┌────────────┐ │          │
│  │  │ Camera   │ │ IoT      │ │ OPC-UA     │ │          │
│  │  │ Sensor   │ │ Stream   │ │ MQTT       │ │          │
│  │  └──────────┘ └──────────┘ └────────────┘ │          │
│  └────────────────────────────────────────────┘          │
│                          │                                │
│  ┌───────────────────────▼───────────────────────────────┐│
│  │    Knowledge Graphs │ Optimization Energy              ││
│  │    GraphDB/RDF      │ Engine                           ││
│  └─────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────────┘│
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Project Structure

```
blender_cv/
├── README.md                      # This file - Project overview
├── README.org                     # Org mode documentation
├── sys_sync.sh                    # System synchronization script
├── pi_config/                     # MCP agent configuration

├── media/                         # Output images/videos

└── video_to_3d/                   # Video reconstruction pipelines
```

## Hardware Requirements


## Hardware Stack Architecture
- **Storage:** 32GB SSD (expandable to 1TB+ for media)


## Hardware Stack Architecture

### Core Edge Computing (Primary Targets)
- **NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano** (4GB/8GB RAM) - Primary deployment target
  - JetPack 6.x with TensorRT acceleration
  - Real-time inference (≤100ms latency)
  - Container isolation for multiple services

- **NVIDIA RTX 5060** (desktop) - Alternative for offline rendering
  - High-throughput batch processing
  - 3D scene reconstruction
  - FEM simulation visualization

### Edge IoT Devices (Distributed Sensing)
- **ESP32** (IoT Cameras, MQTT Broker Nodes)
  - WiFi/BLE enabled
  - Deep sleep mode for power efficiency
  - RGB, thermal, depth cameras
  - MQTT pub/sub capabilities
  - Microphone arrays for audio
  - Accelerometer + gyroscope sensors
  - Custom PCB mounting options

- **Arduino Uno R4** (Controller Applications)
  - WiFi & BLE modules
  - Real-time control logic
  - I2C/SPI sensors integration
  - Servo motor drivers
  - ADC for analog signals
  - CAN bus support

- **Raspberry Pi Zero W/2 W** (Lightweight Edge Nodes)
  - Pi Camera Module support
  - CSI camera interfaces
  - LoRaWAN expansion
  - GPIO sensor arrays
  - Lightweight inference (quantized models)

- **Raspberry Pi Pico/Pico 2** (Microcontroller Edge)
  - RP2040 dual-core ARM
  - 125MHz-133MHz CPU
  - PWM control (motors, servos)
  - I2C/SPI sensor buses
  - BLE/UART communication
  - Deep sleep support

- **Raspberry Pi 4/5** (Workstation Deployment)
  - Full desktop applications
  - Multiple CSI camera inputs
  - FEM simulation rendering
  - Docker container hosting
  - High-bandwidth SSD storage

- **M5Stack** (Modular Sensors Platform)
  - ESP32-WROOM + ATwin module
  - AI Kit with Coral TPU
  - LIDAR + cameras
  - Depth cameras (ToF)
  - Accelerometer + gyroscope
  - Microphone array
  - LoRa + WiFi + BLE

### Camera Modules Supported
- **CSI Cameras** (Native Jetson)
  - IMX219 (standard RGB)
  - IMX477 (global shutter)
  - IMX335 (wide angle)
  - IMX415 (depth/3D)
  - RGB + IR + Thermal multi-sensor
  - 4K @ 60fps capable

- **USB Cameras** (Fallback/Development)
  - Logitech C920/C930
  - Intel RealSense D435
  - Microsoft Kinect (legacy)
  - Micro USB cameras

- **ESP32 Cameras** (IoT Vision Nodes)
  - OV2640 (VGA, low cost)
  - OV7670 + V2
  - OV8865 (WVGA, color)
  - MIPI interface options

- **M5Stack Cameras** (Depth Sensing)
  - TOF depth camera
  - RGB depth array
  - 3D point cloud output

### Camera Integration Features
- **Multi-camera fusion** - Sensor data merging
- **Camera calibration** - Intrinsics/Extrinsics
- **Color correction** - White balance
- **HDR processing** - Tone mapping
- **Exposure control** - Auto/manual
- **Focus distance** - Near/far focus
- **Frame rate control** - FPS throttling
- **Buffer management** - Circular queues

### Hardware Communication Interfaces

- **I2C** - Sensor data reading (IMU, temp, pressure)
- **SPI** - Camera modules, display panels
- **UART** - Serial console, BLE dongles
- **GPIO** - Digital I/O, PWM control
- **CAN Bus** - Automotive-grade control
- **Ethernet** - High-bandwidth networking
- **WiFi/BLE** - Wireless sensor networks
- **LoRa** - Low power long-range

### Resource Requirements by Deployment

| Device | RAM | GPU | CPU | Storage |
|--------|-----|-----|-----|---------|
| Jetson Orin | 8GB | 120 TOPS | 4x A76AE | NVMe SSD |
| RTX 5060 | 16GB+ | 6GB GDDR6 | 6-core CPU | |
| Raspberry Pi | 4GB | CPU-only | Quad-core | SD/NVMe |
| ESP32 | 520KB | N/A | Tenspeed | Flash |
| Arduino | 2KB | N/A | N/A | Flash |
| M5Stack | 520KB | Coral TPU | 4GB eMMC | |

### Storage Recommendations
- **NVMe SSD** - Primary models/data (32GB+ minimum)
- **SD Card** - Backup for Pi devices (16GB+ Class 10)
- **USB Flash** - Portable configuration files
- **HDD** - Archival media (8TB+ recommended)

## Hardware Requirements

### Minimum Resources
- **Jetson:** 8GB RAM, JetPack 6.x
- **PC Workstation:** 16GB RAM, 4GB+ GPU
- **Edge Nodes:** 4GB+ (Raspberry Pi/Zero)
- **MCU Nodes:** 520KB+ (ESP32/Pico)

## Core Components

### 1. Computer Vision Pipeline (`camera_py/`, `camera/`)

Real-time pose estimation using TensorRT-accelerated models:

- **pose_estimate_py/** - PyTorch/Ultralytics training & export
  - Train custom pose models with YOLO11n-pose
  - Export to ONNX for TensorRT conversion
  - Batch processing with queue management

- **pose_estimate_of/** - OpenFrameworks C++ for high-performance inference
  - ONNX runtime integration
  - Low-latency deployment

- **model/** - Model artifacts storage:
  - `.pt` - PyTorch models (training)
  - `.onnx` - ONNX Intermediate format
  - `.engine` - TensorRT optimized engines

**Features:**
- CSI camera support (IMX219, RGB, thermal)
- Real-time inference (≤100ms latency)
- Zoom, pan, flip controls
- Photo/video capture
- Histogram and vectorscope displays

### 2. Finite Element Analysis (`heat_fem/`)

Thermal and structural simulations using FEniCSx/DOLPHIN:

- **FEM Mesh** - Adaptive mesh refinement
- **Thermal Analysis** - Heat transfer, conduction, radiation
- **Structural** - Stress, strain, deformation
- **Optimization** - Topology optimization for lightweight designs

**Features:**
- HDF5 output for large datasets
- 30-minute solver timeout
- Mesh quality validation
- Parallel computation (8 cores max)

### 3. Physics Optimization (`phys_opt/`)

Constraint-based optimization engines:

- **Pyomo** - Mathematical modeling
- **IPOPT** - Interior-point optimization
- **Result caching** - 24-hour cache
- **Multi-physics** - Thermal + structural + fluid

### 4. Visualization & 3D (`blender_cv/`, `video_to_3d/`)

3D modeling and rendering:

- **Blender integration** - 3D scene assembly
- **ONNX models** - Direct export to 3D
- **WebGL** - Web-based 3D viewers
- **Export formats** - .obj, .fbx, .glb

### 5. IoT & Sensor Integration

Real-world data ingestion:

- **MQTT** - MQTT broker for sensor pub/sub
- **OPC-UA** - Industrial device integration
- **CoAP** - Lightweight MQTT alternative
- **Sensor fusion** - Multi-sensor data merging
- **Data streams** - High-frequency telemetry

### 6. Edge Computing & Deployment

On-prem deployment capabilities:

- **JetPack 6.x** - NVIDIA accelerated runtime
- **TensorRT** - GPU-accelerated inference
- **ONNX Runtime** - CPU GPU interoperability
- **Model optimization** - Quantization, pruning for edge
- **Docker/Kubernetes** - Container orchestration
- **sys_sync.sh** - System synchronization script

## Quick Start

### 1. Environment Setup

```bash
# Load CUDA environment
export CUDA_HOME=/usr/local/cuda
export PATH=$CUDA_HOME/bin:$PATH
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=$CUDA_HOME/lib64:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH
export CPATH=$CUDA_HOME/include:$CPATH

source ~/.bashrc
```

### 2. Install Dependencies

```bash
# System packages
sudo apt install python3-opencv python3-numpy

# Python packages
cd camera
pip install -r requirements.txt

# Configure camera (CSI)
sudo /opt/nvidia/jetson-io/jetson-io.py
```

### 3. Build Models

```bash
# Train pose model
cd pose_estimate_py
python train.py

# Export to ONNX
model.export(format='onnx')
mv model.onnx ../model/

# Create TensorRT engine
cd ../camera
python build_engine.py
```

### 4. Run Application

```bash
cd camera
python -m camera.camera_controller

# Or use Docker
docker compose up -d
```

### 5. Deploy Digital Twin

```bash
# Start all services
docker compose up -d

# Check status
docker compose ps

# View logs
docker compose logs -f
```

This folder contains all the knowledge base and presentation for the Jetson CV Digital Twin project.

## Purpose

- **knowledge base**: Raw markdown documentation about hardware, software, add-ons, packages, and system components
- **html**: Converted web pages and slides for public presentation
- **plan**: Agentic orchestration for documentation generation
- **script**: Tools to convert markdown to HTML slides and blog posts
- **static_html**: Final web pages ready for publishing

## Documentation Pipeline

```
knowledge_base/*.md ─[./script/convert_md.sh]──> static_html/*.html
                      │                          │
                      ▼                          ▼
                  mermaid/diagrams           Blog posts index
```

### Workflow

1. `knowledge_base/*.md` - Write documentation in markdown
2. `script/org2slide.py` - Convert `.org` presentations to HTML slides
3. `script/convert_md.sh` - Standard markdown to HTML conversion
4. `static_html/` - Ready-to-publish web pages

## Files to Convert

### Core Documentation (priority order)

1. **project_details.md** - Main README
   - Architecture overview
   - Hardware stack
   - Digital twin capabilities

2. **agent_configs/** - MCP agent documentation
   - System policies
   - Agent roles
   - Available skills

3. **hardware_docs/** - Hardware architecture
   - Jetson targets
   - Camera modules
   - IoT devices

4. **software_docs/** - System components
   - Vision pipeline
   - FEM solver
   - Optimization engines

### Presentation Files

- `org2slide.py` - Converts org-mode to HTML slides
- `slide_presentation.org` - Sample presentation file

## Static Web Pages Structure

### HTML Pages

```
static_html/
├── index.html              # Landing page
├── architecture.html       # Architecture diagrams
├── hardware.html           # Hardware specifications
├── software.html           # Software components
├── deployment.html         # Deployment guides
├── examples/               # Use cases
│   ├── digital_twin.html
│   ├── thermal_analysis.html
│   └── pose_estimation.html
├── blog/                   # Blog posts index
│   └── index.html
├── docs/                   # Reference documentation
└── assets/
    ├── css/
    ├── img/
    └── js/
```

### Available Static Content

- **icon/** - SVG icons for web elements
- **data/** - JSON datasets for charts/graphs
- **css/** - Style sheets (dark, elegant theme)
- **js/** - D3.js visualizations

## Quick Start

### 1. Create Documentation

Write your markdown in `knowledge_base/`:

```bash
mkdir -p knowledge_base/{hardware,software,agents}
cd knowledge_base
echo "# My Component" > my_component.md
```

### 2. Generate Web Pages

```bash
# Convert markdown to HTML
./script/convert_md.sh knowledge_base/*.md

# Generate presentation slides
python3 ./script/org2slide.py slide_presentation.org

# Build all static content
./script/generate_diagrams.sh
```

### 3. Publish

```bash
cd static_html
git add .
git commit -m "update documentation"
git push
```n
## Conversion Options

### Markdown to HTML

```bash
# Simple conversion
./script/convert_md.sh

# With diagrams
./script/generate_diagrams.sh

# With org2html
python3 ./script/org2slide.py
```

### Diagram Generation

- **Mermaid** - Flowcharts and sequence diagrams
- **Graphviz** - System architecture diagrams
- **D3.js** - Interactive data visualizations

## Theme & Styling

- **Dark theme** - Professional technical documentation
- **Responsive** - Mobile-friendly layout
- **Print-friendly** - PDF generation ready
- **Accessible** - WCAG 2.1 compliant

- **NVIDIA Jetson**: https://developer.nvidia.com/jetson
- **TensorRT**: https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/tensorrt/
- **ONNX**: https://onnx.ai/
- **Blender**: https://www.blender.org/
